A1.justification: Both 13-page PDFs describe DVGT and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite editorial and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–6 report original DVGT reconstruction, depth-estimation, ego-pose, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original DVGT evaluations across five driving datasets and the coordinate-scaling and attention ablations in Tables 1–6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same image encoder, factorized attention, ego-token aggregation, prediction heads, pseudo-label construction, and training losses. No algorithmic or architectural component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes, KITTI, OpenScene, Waymo, and DDAD for the same reconstruction, depth, and ego-pose tasks. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1–4. Tables 1–2 retain CUT3R, VGGT, MapAnything, StreamVGGT, and Driv3R; Table 3 retains its four comparators, and Table 4 retains the same six depth-estimation baselines.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, 2 Hz sampling, training budget, image preprocessing, dynamic frame/view sampling, evaluation metrics, and alignment procedures are unchanged. Appendices A, B, and D and Table 7 preserve the same settings.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 retain the same coordinate-scaling and attention ablations. The pseudo-label failure analysis and qualitative reconstruction comparisons also retain the same questions, cases, and findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. For example, DVGT's nuScenes ray-depth Abs Rel remains 0.069 and its δ < 1.25 accuracy remains 0.953. The qualitative figures retain the same cases and findings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), including the model formulation, losses, and metric definitions, retain the same mathematics. Equation (13) moves from PDF page 12 to page 13 without modification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about metric-scaled reconstruction from unposed images, independence from explicit camera parameters, adaptability across camera configurations, and performance advantages.

C2.justification: The explanations for weaker Waymo reconstruction and KITTI pose performance, pseudo-label failure conditions, and attention efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs are unchanged. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: The disclosed architecture, hyperparameters, preprocessing, 64-H20 training setup, and approximately six-day training time are unchanged. Code and project access statements are also retained; the training-time sentence receives only a wording edit.

R1.justification: v2 adds GaussianAD, Doe-1, and PointOcc references and removes Driving in the Occupancy World. These limited supporting-citation changes leave the substantive positioning against occupancy methods and general visual geometry models unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and author-role designations, adds Acknowledgements, removes Appendix E on author contributions, and lightly rephrases the training-time sentence. The scientific prose and main section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3, 5, and 7 use higher-resolution versions of existing imagery with small crop or spacing adjustments. References and appendices reflow, including Figure 8 and Equation (13), and page-number footers disappear. Table structures and figure findings are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the methods, numerical evidence, analyses, and reproducibility information. Sharper figure exports and added funding disclosure provide modest benefits, while removing Appendix E reduces contributor-role transparency. These limited editorial tradeoffs leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
